_comment: Tuning parameters for recommendation_engine. Scoring code reads every number from here; change values, not code. Validated by recommendation_engine/config/__init__.py on load.

history._comment: order_sources: which orders.source values count as purchase history. Subscription orders are excluded on purpose: their cadence is set by the subscription itself, so feeding them back would just confirm our own suggestion. reference_date: 'latest_order_date' (newest order of those sources; the synthetic history ends 2026-11-15), 'today', or a fixed ISO date. An explicit as_of argument always wins.

eligibility._comment: Only products the customer has bought are ever recommended. exclude_live_subscriptions: hide products the customer already subscribes to (subscriptions.status not in inactive_subscription_statuses).

weighted_median._comment: Recency weighting of purchase intervals: weight = 0.5 ** (age / half_life_intervals), age 0 = newest interval. null half-life = equal weights (plain weighted median). max_intervals: only the most recent N intervals are used (null = all).

weights._comment: FinalScore = due * DueScore + habit * HabitScore + consistency * ConsistencyScore. Must sum to 1.

fallbacks._comment: Scores used inside FinalScore when the real score cannot be measured. The API still reports the real score as null and lists the fallback in fallbacks_applied.

habit._comment: HabitScore = min(1, purchase_occasions / threshold). category_field: the products column whose value selects the threshold. consumption_pattern is used because BigBasket's 'category' lumps daily milk with fortnightly butter. Unknown or missing values use default.

consistency._comment: ConsistencyScore = 1 / (1 + CV), CV = std(intervals) / mean(intervals). std_ddof 1 = sample standard deviation.

replenishment_status._comment: Classified from DueScore. At DueScore 1, DueRatio (days since last purchase / expected interval) separates Due from Overdue: Overdue once DueRatio > overdue_ratio.

lapse._comment: Lapsed habits. DueScore is capped at 1, so on its own a product the customer stopped buying months ago would rank as high as one due today. Once days since the last purchase exceed lapse_start = max(start_ratio * expected_interval, expected_interval + min_extra_days), the product is 'Lapsed' and FinalScore is multiplied by lapse_factor = max(floor, 0.5 ** (intervals_past_lapse_start / half_life_intervals)). min_extra_days keeps a short holiday from marking fast products (milk every 2 days) as lapsed. enabled=false restores the plain formula.

quantity._comment: Suggested quantity = median units per purchase occasion, rounded half up, never below min_quantity.

explanations._comment: Wording thresholds only; they never change scores.
